---
title: "Layers and Lines"
---

An SVG draws later elements on top of earlier ones. shinymap uses that to keep
important outlines visible: it draws the map in layers, and it redraws selected and
hovered regions on top so that their borders are never covered by a neighbour.

## The layers, bottom to top

Each picture adds one layer to the previous one.

::: {layout-ncol=5}
![1. underlay](../images/generated/layer-1-underlay.svg){fig-alt="A light blue background rectangle" width="100%"}

![2. base](../images/generated/layer-2-base.svg){fig-alt="Hexagon grid on the background" width="100%"}

![3. overlay](../images/generated/layer-3-overlay.svg){fig-alt="A blue river line drawn over the grid" width="100%"}

![4. selection](../images/generated/layer-4-select.svg){fig-alt="Two selected hexagons drawn over the river" width="100%"}

![5. hover](../images/generated/layer-5-hover.svg){fig-alt="A hovered hexagon outlined above everything" width="100%"}
:::

| Layer | What goes there | Clickable |
|---|---|---|
| underlay | backgrounds, sea, frames | no |
| base | the regions users click | **yes** |
| overlay | borders, dividers, rivers, grids | no |
| selection | copies of the selected regions, in the select look | no (clicks pass through) |
| hover | a copy of the hovered region, in the hover look | no (clicks pass through) |
| annotation | labels and marks that must stay on top of everything | no |

Regions in the `hidden` layer are not drawn at all.

## Putting regions on a layer

A region's layer is recorded in the outline's metadata; its ID does not matter. Use
`move_layer` to set it:

```python
outline = (
    Outline.from_svg("map.svg")
    .move_layer("underlay", "_background")
    .move_layer("overlay", "_river", "_borders")
)
```

`layers=` on `input_map()` / `output_map()` does the same for one map:
`layers={"overlay": ["_river"]}`. The keys are singular: `underlay`, `overlay`,
`annotation`, `hidden`.

## Lines need `path_as_line`

An SVG `<path>` can be a filled shape or a line; the path data alone does not say
which. Unless told otherwise, shinymap fills paths as shapes. An open path such as a
river then turns into a filled area:

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![Without `path_as_line`](../images/generated/line-as-shape.svg){fig-alt="The river path filled in gray, covering part of the grid" width="100%"}

![With `path_as_line("_river")`](../images/generated/line-as-line.svg){fig-alt="The river drawn as a blue line" width="100%"}
:::

```python
outline = outline.path_as_line("_river").move_layer("overlay", "_river")
```

Lines get the line look (`aes.Line`, or `Wash(line=...)`) and no fill. The sketch app
(`python -m shinymap.kit.sketch`) suggests likely lines for you: open paths and paths
with `fill="none"`.
